page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 24 dedicated virtual CPU cores alongside 96.0 GB of system memory. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core, the hardware architecture is built to support broad enterprise software stacks that demand proportional compute and memory scaling without tipping toward specialized memory or compute configurations.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring persistence to be provisioned via remote block storage. It also contains no hardware accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, but provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. From a qualitative resource-efficiency standpoint, the dedicated 24-core allocation avoids noisy-neighbor contention, making it cost-efficient for medium-to-large multi-threaded enterprise services, relational databases, backend web serving fleets, enterprise resource planning systems, and batch processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.6xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance based on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. Equipped with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, it supplies 24 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of RAM, adhering strictly to a balanced 1:4 memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server has no integrated local storage or GPU accelerators, directing primary I/O through external cloud storage across an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are attached by default. Designed to deliver predictable dedicated compute capacity without the overhead of asymmetric memory or accelerator hardware, the ecs.g6.6xlarge suits standard enterprise production workloads, including relational database management systems, distributed application backends, container orchestration nodes, continuous integration pipelines, and general enterprise application hosting.
